Both definitions require a neighbourhood on which the module is generated by finitely many sections, equivalently a quotient of a finite free module.
Stacks gives global Hom and the local-Hom presheaf for modules on a commutative ringed space; the source is formulated for left modules over a possibly noncommutative sheaf of rings.
The property historically called pseudo-coherent here is exactly the current Stacks finite-presentation condition: locally a cokernel of a map between finite free modules.
Both definitions mean that every open covering admits a finite subcover, without a Hausdorff requirement.
Stacks constructs the same sheaf U mapping to Hom over O|U in the commutative ringed-space setting; the source permits a noncommutative ring sheaf and initially obtains an abelian-group sheaf.

Stacks proves the sheafification formula for the special functor f_*; the source gives the same localization formula for the right derived functors of an arbitrary sheaf-valued functor T.
The Stacks lemma says every positive-degree cohomology class dies on an open cover; taking the member containing x gives exactly the asserted smaller neighbourhood.
Stacks proves restriction to an open preserves injectives and that its derived section functors compute H^q of that open, exactly as here.
The Stacks product-over-points sheaf has surjective restriction projections and is therefore flasque; the cited Cech lemma then gives precisely the claimed vanishing for every cover.
Stacks constructs the same functorial map from fixed-cover Cech cohomology to derived sheaf cohomology.

The corrected direction agrees with the Stacks cochain map from a coarser cover complex to a refinement, functorial in the sheaf and compatible under composition.
